title: Contributing to modsem
text: Thank considering contributing modsem! welcome contributions help improve package estimating interaction effects structural equation modeling (SEM). ensure smooth collaboration, please follow guidelines .

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Fork repository GitHub. Clone fork local machine.
code: git clone https://github.com/your-username/modsem.git cd modsem

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Ensure R installed machine. Install package dependencies. Install modsem package local repository.
code: install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_deps() devtools::install()

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Always create new branch work.
code: git checkout -b your-branch-name

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Make changes codebase. Ensure changes well-documented. Write tests changes applicable.

title: Contributing to modsem
text: also encourage contributions vignettes. new use case example, feel free add alter vignettes help demonstrate functionality modsem.

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Run tests ensure changes break existing functionality.
code: devtools::test()

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Push changes fork. Open pull request GitHub main branch original repository.
code: git push origin your-branch-name

title: Contributing to modsem
text: Provide clear descriptive title pull request. Describe changes made necessary. Reference related issues pull requests. Ensure tests pass merge conflicts.

title: Contributing to modsem
text: encounter issues suggestions improvements, please open issue GitHub. Provide much detail possible help us understand address issue.

title: composite constructs
text: version 1.0.20, modsem function supports estimation models composite constructs, using method="lms". approach based Tamara Schamberger, Florian Schuberth, Jörg Henseler & Yves Rosseel, 2015. Depending lavaan version (>=0.6-20), composite constructs can also used product indicator approaches (e.g., method="dblcent"). can see simple example, using LMS approach TPB dataset.

att4 + att5   BEH <~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC + INT:PBC '  fit <- modsem(tpb, TPB, method = "lms", nodes = 32) summary(fit) #> title: customizing the output from `plot_interaction()`
text: fit simple model, create baseline plot, ’ll customize.
code: library(modsem) #> This is modsem (1.0.24). Please report any bugs! library(ggplot2)  m <- ' X =~ x1 + x2 + x3 Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3 Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3  Y ~ X + Z + X:Z '  fit <- modsem(m, data = oneInt, method = "lms") p <- plot_interaction(x = "X", z = "Z", y = "Y", vals_z = c(-1, 1), model = fit) print(p)

title: customizing the output from `plot_interaction()`
text: Changing legend title bit trickier, can done using guides() function. Since plot_interaction() uses fill color aesthetic, must specified, title.
code: p + guides(fill=guide_legend(title = "New Legend Title"),            color=guide_legend(title = "New Legend Title"))

title: customizing the output from `plot_interaction()`
text: ggplot2 comes different color palettes, can use replace default color palette. numerous options (can also download additional packages), can see examples using brewer palettes. see available palettes can run snippet.  example using Dark2 palette.  example using Accent palette.

title: customizing the output from `plot_interaction()`
text: Changing linetypes compliacted changing colors plot. add whole new aesthetic plot. can done using aes() function. Behind scenes, modsem uses variable cat_z form groups output plot_interaction, pass linetype = cat_z. can see unfortunate side effect, created second Legend plot. can however fixed renaming Legend title (see Legend Title section).

text: can see example combining different options.
code: p +   ggtitle("Customized Plot") + # New Title   xlab("Values of X") + # New X-axis label   ylab("Predicted values of Y") + # New y-axis label   scale_color_grey() + # Add Grey theem   scale_fill_grey() +   aes(linetype = cat_z) + # Add linetypes   guides(color    = guide_legend("Values of Z"), # Change Legend Title          fill     = guide_legend("Values of Z"),          linetype = guide_legend("Values of Z"))

title: customizing interaction terms
text: default, modsem() creates possible combinations product indicators. title: estimation alternatives using the LMS approach
text: default (v1.0.9) LMS approach uses accelerated EM procedure ("EMA") uses Quasi-Newton Fisher Scoring optimization steps needed. desirable, can switched standard Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, setting algorithm = "EM". default LMS approach also uses quasi-adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, estimate numerical approximation log-likelihood. Due performance reasons, adaptive quadrature fit individual quadrature participant, instead one entire sample (EM iteration), based whole sample densities likelihood function. essentially works removing irrelevant nodes don’t contribute integral, increasing number nodes actually contribute integral. usually means nodes placed towards center distribution, compared standard fixed Gauss-Hermite quadrature. Using EMA adaptive quadrature might yield estimates closer results Mplus. fixed Gauss-Hermite quadrature can used instead, setting adaptive.quad = FALSE. model struggles converge, can try changing EM procedure setting algorithm = "EMA" algorithm = "EM", switching adaptive fixed quadrature (adaptive.quad), increasing number nodes (nodes) modsem() function. Additionally possible tweak parameters: max.iter: Maximum number iterations EM algorithm (default 500). max.step: Maximum number steps used Maximization step EM algorithm (default 1). convergence.rel: Relative convergence criterion EM algorithm (default 1e-10). convergence.abs: Absolute convergence criterion EM algorithm (default 1e-4). convergence.grad: Gradient convergence criterion (default 1e-3). absolute relative criterion reached, estimation stops largest absolute gradient log-likelihood convergence.grad. Otherwise Fisher scoring step taken EM algorithm continues, em.control$grad.max.steps (default 25) steps. Set Inf disable check. nodes: Number nodes numerical integration (default 24). Increasing number can improve accuracy estimates, especially complex models. adaptive.quad: quasi-adaptive quadrature used (default TRUE)? FALSE, fixed Gauss-Hermite quadrature used. quad.range: Integration range quadrature. Smaller ranges means integral focused. Applies using quasi-adaptive quadrature. adaptive.frequency: often quasi-adaptive quadrature calculated? Defaults every third EM iteration. adaptive.quad.tol: Relative error tolerance calculating quasi-adaptive quadrature (default 1e-12). em.control: list control parameters EM EMA algorithms (e.g., grad.max.steps), fine-tuning estimation procedure. n.threads: Number threads used computing densities likelihood function. default (NULL), two threads used, "max" uses available threads. can see example using TPB_UK dataset, troublesome estimate simulated TPB dataset. using quasi-adaptive quadrature (default), Numerical Integration section summary reports two sets node counts. Standard requested number nodes (nodes), roughly number nodes kept pruning. Effective number nodes need fixed Gauss-Hermite quadrature (adaptive.quad = FALSE) get effectively results. information can retrieved using modsem_inspect(fit, "quad").
code: tpb_uk <- " # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3 + pbc4   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3 + int4   BEH =~ beh1 + beh2 + beh3  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ INT:PBC "  fit <- modsem(tpb_uk,               data = TPB_UK,               method = "lms",               nodes = 32, # Number of nodes for numerical integration               adaptive.quad = TRUE, # Use quasi-adaptive quadrature               adaptive.frequency = 3, # Update title: fit measures for LMS and QML
text: vignette demonstrates evaluate compare model fit latent interaction models estimated via Latent Moderated Structural Equations (LMS) approach. Quasi-Maximum Likelihood (QML) approach. using modsem package (v≥1.0.8). standard Chi-square statistics available LMS/QML, assess fit : Examining fit indices baseline (-interaction) model. Conducting likelihood-ratio difference test compare baseline interaction models (Klein & Moosbrugger, 2000; Klein & Múthen, 2007). baseline model shows acceptable fit adding latent interaction significantly improves fit, interaction model can also deemed well-fitting.

title: fit measures for LMS and QML
text: define model three latent variables (X, Y, Z) interaction (X:Z):
code: m1 <- " # Outer (measurement) model X =~ x1 + x2 + x3 Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3 Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3  # Inner (structural) model Y ~ X + Z + X:Z "  # Estimate the full (H1) model via LMS est_h1 <- modsem(m1, oneInt, method = "lms")  # Estimate the baseline (H0) model without interaction est_h0 <- estimate_h0(est_h1, calc.se = FALSE) # std.errors are not needed

title: interaction effects between endogenous variables
text: Interaction effects two endogenous (.e., dependent) variables work expect product indicator methods ("dblcent", "rca", "ca", "uca"). However, lms qml approaches, straightforward. lms qml approaches can (default) handle interaction effects endogenous exogenous (.e., independent) variables, natively support interaction effects two endogenous variables. interaction effect exists two endogenous variables, equations easily written “reduced” form, meaning normal estimation procedures won’t work.

title: interaction effects between endogenous variables
text: Despite limitations, workaround lms qml approaches. Essentially, model can split two parts: one linear one non-linear. can replace covariance matrix used estimation non-linear model model-implied covariance matrix linear model. allows treat endogenous variable exogenous—provided can expressed linear model.

title: interaction effects between endogenous variables
text: Let’s consider theory planned behavior (TPB), wish estimate quadratic effect INT BEH (INT:INT). can use following model: Since INT endogenous variable, quadratic term (.e., interaction effect ) involve two endogenous variables. result, normally able estimate model using lms qml approaches. However, can split model two parts: one linear one non-linear. INT endogenous variable, can expressed linear model since affected interaction terms: can remove part original model, giving us: Now, can estimate non-linear model since INT treated exogenous variable. However, incorporate structural model INT. address , can instruct modsem replace covariance matrix (phi) (INT, PBC, ATT, SN) model-implied covariance matrix linear model estimating models simultaneously. achieve , use cov.syntax argument modsem: also possible make modsem attempt split model syntax automatically using auto.split.syntax argument:
code: tpb <- ' # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ INT:INT ' tpb_linear <- 'INT ~ PBC + ATT + SN' tpb_nonlinear <- ' # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., text: example complex model based theory planned behavior (TPB), includes two endogenous variables interaction endogenous exogenous variable. estimating complex models LMS approach, recommended increase number nodes used numerical integration. default, number nodes set 24, can increased using nodes argument. nodes argument effect QML approach. interaction effect endogenous exogenous variable, recommended use least 32 nodes LMS approach. can also obtain robust standard errors setting robust.se = TRUE modsem() function. NOTE: want LMS approach produce results similar possible Mplus, consider increasing number nodes using nodes argument, using quasi-adaptive quadrature setting adaptive.quad=TRUE.

text: Using LMS QML approaches possible estimate interaction terms means latent variables centered (.e., non-zero means). can see example using TPB dataset: Comparing estimates get PBC INT zero means, see coefficients BEH~PBC BEH~INT drastically changed. bug, function interaction effect rescaling coefficients, centered zero. using standardized_estimates function, summary(est, standardized = TRUE) interaction effect centered, can see coefficients BEH~PBC BEH~INT rescaled . also possible get centered solution using centered_estimates() function. Note, centered_estimates() removes mean structure model together.

title: methods
text: Note constraints can become quite complicated complex models, particularly interaction including enodgenous variables. method can therefore quite slow. "uca" = unconstrained approach (Marsh, 2004) "rca" = residual centering approach (Little et al., 2006) default "pind" = basic product indicator approach (recommended)

title: methods
text: "lms" = Latent Moderated Structural equations (LMS) approach, see vignette "qml" = Quasi Maximum Likelihood (QML) approach, see vignette estimates model Mplus, installed
code: m1 <- ' # Outer Model X =~ x1 + x2 + x3 Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3 Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3  # Inner model Y ~ X + Z + X:Z '  # Product Indicator Approaches modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "ca") modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "uca") modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "rca") modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "dblcent")  # Distribution Analytic Approaches modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "mplus") modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "lms") modsem(m1, data = oneInt, method = "qml")

title: modsem
text: modsem introduces new feature lavaan syntax—semicolon operator (:). semicolon operator works way lm() function. specify interaction effect two variables, join Var1:Var2. Models can estimated using one product indicator approaches ("ca", "rca", "dblcent", "pind") using latent moderated structural equations approach ("lms") quasi maximum likelihood approach ("qml"). product indicator approaches estimated via lavaan, lms qml approaches estimated via modsem .

title: plotting interaction effects
text: Interaction effects can plotted using included plot_interaction() function. function takes fitted model object names two variables interacting. function plot interaction effect two variables, : x-variable plotted x-axis. y-variable plotted y-axis. z-variable determines points effect x y plotted. function also plot 95% confidence interval interaction effect. Note vals_z argument (well values x) scaled mean standard deviation variables. Unless rescale argument set FALSE. simple example using double-centering approach:  different example using lms approach theory planned behavior model:
code: m1 <- " # Outer Model   X =~ x1 + x2 + x3   Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3   Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3  # Inner Model   Y ~ X + Z + X:Z " est1 <- modsem(m1, data = oneInt) plot_interaction(x = "X", z = "Z", y = "Y",                  vals_z = -3:3, model = est1) tpb <- " # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ PBC:INT "  est2 <- modsem(tpb, TPB, method = "lms") plot_interaction(x = "INT", z = "PBC", y = "BEH",                  vals_z = c(-0.5, 0.5), model = est2)

title: plotting interaction effects
text: plot_jn() function can used plot Johnson-Neyman regions given interaction effect. function takes fitted model object, names two variables interacting, name interaction effect. function plot Johnson-Neyman regions interaction effect. plot_jn() function also plot 95% confidence interval interaction effect. x name x-variable, z name z-variable, y name y-variable. model fitted model object. argument min_z max_z used specify range values moderating variable. example using ca approach Holzinger-Swineford (1939) dataset:  another example using qml approach theory planned behavior model:
code: m1 <-  '   visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3   textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6   speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9    visual ~ speed + textual + speed:textual '  est1 <- modsem(m1, data = lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939, method = "ca") plot_jn(x = "speed", z = "textual", y = "visual", model = est1, max_z = 6) #> Johnson-Neyman regions: #>   When textual <= -1.52, the direct effect of speed is not significant (p >= .05). #>   When textual is between -1.52 and 5.20, the direct effect of speed is p < .05. #>   When textual >= 5.20, the direct effect of speed is not significant (p >= .05). tpb <- " # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ PBC:INT "  est2 <- modsem(tpb, TPB, method = "qml") plot_jn(x = "INT", z = "PBC", y = "BEH", model = est2,         min_z = -1.5, max_z = -0.5) #> Johnson-Neyman regions: #>   When PBC <= -1.24, the direct effect of INT is p < .05. #>   When PBC is between -1.24 and -0.67, the direct effect of INT is not significant (p >= .05). #>   When PBC >= -0.67, the direct effect of INT is p < .05. #> Warning: modsem->plotJN_Group():   #>    Truncating SD-range on the right and left!

title: plotting interaction effects
text: plot_surface() function can used plot 3D surface plots given interaction effect. function takes fitted model object, names two variables interacting, name dependent variable. function plot 3D surface plot interaction effect.
code: tpb <- " # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ PBC:INT "  est2 <- modsem(tpb, TPB, method = "qml") plot_surface(x = "INT", z = "PBC", y = "BEH", model = est2)

code: set.seed(2934269)  var_X      <- 1 var_Z      <- 1 cov_X_Z    <- 0.2  zeta_Y     <- 0.4  gamma_Y_X  <-  0 gamma_Y_Z  <-  0 gamma_Y_XZ <-  1 gamma_Y_ZZ <-  3 # exclude for now gamma_Y_XX <- -1 # exclude for now   lambda_1   <- 1 lambda_2   <- .7 lambda_3   <- .8   epsilon    <- 0.2 beta_1     <- 1.2 beta_2     <- 0.8 beta_3     <- 1.5 N          <- 1500  residual <- \(epsilon) rnorm(N, sd = sqrt(epsilon)) create_ind <- \(lv, beta, lambda, epsilon) beta + lambda * lv + residual(epsilon)   Phi <- matrix(c(var_X, cov_X_Z,                 cov_X_Z, var_Z), nrow = 2) XI <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(N, sigma = Phi)  X <- XI[, 1] Z <- XI[, 2]  Y <-   gamma_Y_X * X +   gamma_Y_Z * Z +   gamma_Y_XZ * X * Z +   gamma_Y_XX * X * X +   gamma_Y_ZZ * Z * Z +   residual(zeta_Y)  x1 <- create_ind(X, beta_1, lambda_1, epsilon) x2 <- create_ind(X, beta_2, lambda_2, epsilon) x3 <- create_ind(X, beta_3, lambda_2, epsilon)  z1 <- create_ind(Z, beta_1, lambda_1, epsilon) z2 <- create_ind(Z, beta_2, lambda_2, epsilon) z3 <- create_ind(Z, beta_3, lambda_2, epsilon)  y1 <- create_ind(Y, beta_1, lambda_1, epsilon) y2 <- create_ind(Y, beta_2, lambda_2, epsilon) y3 <- create_ind(Y, beta_2, lambda_2, epsilon)   data.sim <- data.frame(    x1, x2, x3,    z1, z2, z3,    y1, y2, y3 )

title: interaction effects in random intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs)
code: library(mvtnorm) set.seed(235910)  N <- 10000  # Simulate between-person random intercepts phi <- matrix(c(   0.806, 0.481, 0.438,   0.481, 0.758, 0.469,   0.438, 0.469, 1.290 ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  Xi <- rmvnorm(   N,   mean = c(0, 0, 0),   sigma = phi )  RIemo <- Xi[, 1] RIper <- Xi[, 2] RIcon <- Xi[, 3]   # Time 3 psi3 <- matrix(c(   1.234, 0.328, 0.478,   0.328, 1.614, 0.427,   0.478, 0.427, 2.743 ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  zeta3 <- rmvnorm(   N,   mean = c(0, 0, 0),   sigma = psi3 )  wemo_3 <- zeta3[, 1] wper_3 <- zeta3[, 2] wcon_3 <- zeta3[, 3]   # Time 5 psi5 <- matrix(c(   1.489, 0.397, 0.301,   0.397, 1.143, 0.202,   0.301, 0.202, 0.764 ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  zeta5 <- rmvnorm(   N,   mean = c(0, 0, 0),   sigma = psi5 )  wemo_5 <- 0.142 * wemo_3 + 0.071 * wper_3 + 0.086 * wcon_3 - 0.010 * (wcon_3 * wper_3) + zeta5[,1] wper_5 <- 0.018 * wemo_3 + 0.100 * wper_3 + 0.050 * wcon_3 + zeta5[,2] wcon_5 <- -0.008 * wemo_3 + 0.006 * wper_3 + 0.105 * wcon_3 + zeta5[,3]  # Time 7 psi7 <- matrix(c(   1.808, 0.521, 0.475,   0.521, 1.287, 0.311,   0.475, 0.311, 0.881 ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  zeta7 <- rmvnorm(   N,   mean = c(0, 0, 0),   sigma = psi7 )  wemo_7 <- 0.361 * wemo_5 + 0.097 * wper_5 + 0.147 * wcon_5 + 0.105 * (wcon_5 * wper_5) + zeta7[,1] wper_7 <- 0.030 * wemo_5 + 0.348 * wper_5 + 0.123 * wcon_5 + zeta7[,2] wcon_7 <- 0.074 * wemo_5 + 0.056 * wper_5 + 0.086 * wcon_5 + zeta7[,3]  # Indicators/Observed Variables data <- data.frame(   emo_3 = 1.385 + RIemo + wemo_3 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   emo_5 = 1.407 + RIemo + wemo_5 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   emo_7 = 1.528 + RIemo + wemo_7 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),    per_3 = 1.563 + RIper + wper_3 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   per_5 = 1.176 + RIper + wper_5 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   per_7 = 1.242 + RIper + wper_7 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),    con_3 = 2.827 + RIcon + wcon_3 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   con_5 = 1.517 + RIcon + wcon_5 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)),   con_7 = 1.402 + RIcon + wcon_7 + rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(.200)) )

code: library(modsem)  m1 <- '   # Outer Model   X =~ x1 + x2 + x3   Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3   Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3      # Inner model   Y ~ X + Z + X:Z  '  # Double centering approach est1_dca <- modsem(m1, oneInt) summary(est1_dca)  # Constrained approach est1_ca <- modsem(m1, oneInt, method = "ca") summary(est1_ca)  # QML approach  est1_qml <- modsem(m1, oneInt, method = "qml") summary(est1_qml, standardized = TRUE)   # LMS approach  est1_lms <- modsem(m1, oneInt, method = "lms")  summary(est1_lms)

title: Latent Interaction (and Moderation) Analysis in Structural Equation Models (SEM)
code: tpb <- " # Outer Model (Based on Hagger et al., 2007)   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model (Based on Steinmetz et al., 2011)   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ PBC:INT "  # double centering approach est_tpb_dca <- modsem(tpb, data = TPB, method = "dblcent") summary(est_tpb_dca)  # Constrained approach using Wrigths path tracing rules for generating # the appropriate constraints est_tpb_ca <- modsem(tpb, data = TPB, method = "ca")  summary(est_tpb_ca)  # LMS approach  est_tpb_lms <- modsem(tpb, data = TPB, method = "lms") summary(est_tpb_lms, standardized = TRUE)   # QML approach  est_tpb_qml <- modsem(tpb, data = TPB, method = "qml")  summary(est_tpb_qml, standardized = TRUE)

what: modsem: Latent Interaction (and Moderation) Analysis in Structural Equation Models (SEM) — modsem-package
title: modsem: Latent Interaction (and Moderation) Analysis in Structural Equation Models (SEM) — modsem-package
text: Estimation interaction (.e., moderation) effects latent variables structural equation models (SEM). supported methods : constrained approach (Algina & Moulder, 2001). unconstrained approach (Marsh et al., 2004). residual centering approach (Little et al., 2006). double centering approach (Lin et al., 2010). latent moderated structural equations (LMS) approach (Klein & Moosbrugger, 2000). quasi-maximum likelihood (QML) approach (Klein & Muthén, 2007) constrained- unconstrained, residual- double centering- approaches estimated via 'lavaan' (Rosseel, 2012), whilst LMS- QML- approaches estimated via 'modsem' self. Alternatively model can estimated via 'Mplus' (Muthén & Muthén, 1998-2017). References: Algina, J., & Moulder, B. C. (2001). doi:10.1207/S15328007SEM0801_3 . "note estimating Jöreskog-Yang model latent variable interaction using 'LISREL' 8.3." Klein, ., & Moosbrugger, H. (2000). doi:10.1007/BF02296338 . "Maximum likelihood estimation latent interaction effects LMS method." Klein, . G., & Muthén, B. O. (2007). doi:10.1080/00273170701710205 . "Quasi-maximum likelihood estimation structural equation models multiple interaction quadratic effects." Lin, G. C., Wen, Z., Marsh, H. W., & Lin, H. S. (2010). doi:10.1080/10705511.2010.488999 . "Structural equation models latent interactions: Clarification orthogonalizing double-mean-centering strategies." Little, T. D., Bovaird, J. ., & Widaman, K. F. (2006). doi:10.1207/s15328007sem1304_1 . "merits orthogonalizing powered product terms: Implications modeling interactions among latent variables." Marsh, H. W., Wen, Z., & Hau, K. T. (2004). doi:10.1037/1082-989X.9.3.275 . "Structural equation models latent interactions: evaluation alternative estimation strategies indicator construction." Muthén, L.K. Muthén, B.O. (1998-2017). "'Mplus' User’s Guide. Eighth Edition." https://www.statmodel.com/. Rosseel Y (2012). doi:10.18637/jss.v048.i02 . "'lavaan': R Package Structural Equation Modeling."

title: Estimate interaction effects in structural equation models (SEMs) — modsem
text: modsem() function estimating interaction effects latent variables structural equation models (SEMs). Methods estimating interaction effects SEMs can basically split two frameworks: Product Indicator (PI) based approaches ("dblcent", "rca", "uca", "ca", "pind") Distributionally (DA) based approaches ("lms", "qml"). product indicator-based approaches, modsem() essentially fancy wrapper lavaan::sem() generates necessary syntax variables estimation models latent product indicators. distributionally based approaches implemented separately estimated using lavaan::sem(), rather using custom functions (largely written C++ performance reasons). greater control, advised use one sub-functions (modsem_pi, modsem_da, modsem_mplus) directly, passing additional arguments via modsem() can lead unexpected behavior.

title: Estimate interaction effects in structural equation models (SEMs) — modsem
code: modsem(model.syntax = NULL, data = NULL, method = "dblcent", ...)

title: Estimate interaction effects in structural equation models (SEMs) — modsem
text: model.syntax lavaan syntax data dataframe method method use: "dblcent" double centering approach (passed lavaan). "ca" constrained approach (passed lavaan). "rca" residual centering approach (passed lavaan). "uca" unconstrained approach (passed lavaan). "pind" prod ind approach, constraints centering (passed lavaan). "lms" latent moderated structural equations (passed lavaan). "qml" quasi maximum likelihood estimation (passed lavaan). "custom" use parameters specified function call (passed lavaan). "mplus" estimate model Mplus. ... arguments passed functions depending method (see modsem_pi, modsem_da, modsem_mplus)

title: Interaction between latent variables using LMS and QML approaches — modsem_da
text: modsem_da() function estimating interaction effects latent variables structural equation models (SEMs) using distributional analytic (DA) approaches. Methods estimating interaction effects SEMs can basically split two frameworks: 1. Product Indicator-based approaches ("dblcent", "rca", "uca", "ca", "pind") 2. Distributionally based approaches ("lms", "qml"). modsem_da() handles latter can estimate models using QML LMS, necessary syntax, variables estimation models latent product indicators. NOTE: Run default_settings_da see default arguments.

title: Interaction between latent variables using product indicators — modsem_pi
text: modsem_pi() function estimating interaction effects latent variables, structural equation models (SEMs), using product indicators. Methods estimating interaction effects SEMs can basically split two frameworks: 1. Product Indicator based approaches ("dblcent", "rca", "uca", "ca", "pind"), 2. Distributionally based approaches ("lms", "qml"). modsem_pi() essentially fancy wrapper lavaan::sem() generates necessary syntax variables estimation models latent product indicators. Use default_settings_pi() get default settings different methods.

title: Plot Interaction Effects in a SEM Model — plot_interaction
text: x character string specifying focal predictor (x-axis variable). z character string specifying moderator variable. y character string specifying outcome (dependent) variable. model object class modsem_pi, modsem_da, modsem_mplus, possibly lavaan object. Must fitted SEM model containing paths y ~ x + z + x:z. vals_x numeric vector values compute plot focal predictor x. default seq(-3, 3, .001), provides relatively fine grid smooth lines. rescale=TRUE, values standardized (mean-centered scaled) units, converted back original metric internal computation predicted means. vals_z numeric vector values moderator z draw separate regression lines. distinct value vals_z defines separate group (plotted different color). rescale=TRUE, values also assumed standardized units. alpha_se numeric value \([0, 1]\) specifying transparency confidence/prediction interval ribbon. Default 0.15. digits integer specifying number decimal places moderator values (z) rounded labeling/grouping plot. ci_width numeric value \((0,1)\) indicating coverage confidence (prediction) interval. default 0.95 95% interval. ci_type character string specifying whether compute "confidence" intervals (mean predicted values, default) "prediction" intervals (include residual variance). rescale Logical. TRUE (default), vals_x vals_z interpreted standardized units, mapped back raw scale computing predictions. FALSE, vals_x vals_z taken raw-scale values directly. standardized coefficients standardized beforehand? xz character string specifying interaction term (x:z). NULL, term created automatically paste(x, z, sep = ":"). SEM backends may handle interaction term differently (instance, removing modifying colon), function attempts reconcile internally. greyscale Logical. TRUE plot plotted greyscale. check.quadratic Logical. TRUE (default), x == z taken mean x moderates , model treated quadratic x. gives single curved line, instead one line per value vals_z (ignored). ... Additional arguments passed simple_slopes.

title: Plot Interaction Effects in a SEM Model — plot_interaction
text: Computation Steps: Calls simple_slopes compute predicted values y         specified grid x z values. Groups resulting predictions unique z-values (rounded         digits) create colored lines. Plots lines using ggplot2, adding ribbons confidence         (prediction) intervals, transparency controlled alpha_se. Interpretation: line plot corresponds regression y x given level z. shaded region around line (ribbon) shows either confidence interval predicted mean (ci_type = "confidence") prediction interval individual observations (ci_type = "prediction"). ribbons overlap, evidence lines differ significantly range x.

title: Plot Interaction Effects in a SEM Model — plot_interaction
code: # \dontrun{ library(modsem)  # Example 1: Interaction of X and Z in a simple SEM m1 <- " # Outer Model   X =~ x1 + x2 + x3   Z =~ z1 + z2 + z3   Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3  # Inner Model   Y ~ X + Z + X:Z " est1 <- modsem(m1, data = oneInt)  # Plot interaction using a moderate range of X and two values of Z plot_interaction(x = "X", z = "Z", y = "Y", xz = "X:Z",                  vals_x = -3:3, vals_z = c(-0.2, 0), model = est1)   # Example 2: Interaction in a theory-of-planned-behavior-style model tpb <- " # Outer Model   ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att5   SN  =~ sn1 + sn2   PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3   INT =~ int1 + int2 + int3   BEH =~ b1 + b2  # Inner Model   INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC   BEH ~ INT + PBC   BEH ~ PBC:INT " est2 <- modsem(tpb, data = TPB, method = "lms", nodes = 32)  # Plot with custom Z values and a denser X grid plot_interaction(x = "INT", z = "PBC", y = "BEH",                  xz = "PBC:INT",                  vals_x = seq(-3, 3, 0.01),                  vals_z = c(-0.5, 0.5),                  model = est2)  # }

text: Estimate interaction model using twostep procedure. PI approaches, lavaan::sam function   used optimize models, instead lavaan::sem. Note product indicators still used,   newly developed SAM approach estimate latent interactions. DA approaches (LMS QML)   measurement model estimated using CFA (lavaan::cfa). structural model estimated using   modsem_da, estimates measurement model fixed, based CFA estimates.   Note standard errors uncorrected (.e., naive), account uncertainty CFA estimates.   NOTE, experimental feature!
